title: Zephyrine and the Typewriter
premise: In the river town of Vellamarch, August Whitlock, a mapmaker's apprentice of no family and fewer loyalties, is secretly finishing the master's forbidden atlas — a document that charts not just roads but every debt, grudge, and hidden allegiance in the province. When the army requisitions the workshop to produce campaign maps, August discovers the ledger of names the atlas was meant to expose has been folded into the requisition itself, and the occupying commander wants the master's work completed under his seal. August must decide whether to finish the atlas truthfully and doom the town's names to the army's reprisals, falsify it and betray the dead master, or destroy a lifetime of work to save the living. As the river ice groans toward its spring break, August completes the atlas one final night, smuggles the true ledger across the thawing water to a rival cartographer's press, and burns the army's copy — surviving the occupation stripped of the master's name, the workshop, and their own assumed identity, but finally owning the one they choose.
about_author: Coral Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing requisitioned municipal records from occupied European towns. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in paperwork's teeth, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unfinished Lines
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the cold workshop of the late Master Odile Ferran, August inks the final coastal plates of her secret atlas, hiding the true ledger of names beneath the floorboards. Establishes August's careful invisibility and grief. Beat: quiet dread — the work is nearly done, and done means dangerous.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: August's POV. Soldiers in gray occupy Vellamarch; a requisition order claims the workshop, the presses, and 'all cartographic materials.' August watches Commander Halvard Renn's clerk inventory the atlas plates and realizes the ledger is listed. Beat: the safe small life ends in an afternoon of stamps and signatures.

chapters.title: The Commander's Seal
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn, a career officer who rose by flattering superiors, orders the atlas finished under army seal to impress the General Staff. He interviews August, mistaking their silence for stupidity. Beat: cold ambition — he sees the atlas as a ladder, not a weapon.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: August's POV. Forced to work beside army draftsmen, August discovers the ledger of names has been interleaved into the requisition files — neighbors, debts, loyalties, all legible to the army. Beat: horror of recognition; the map of home has become a target list.

chapters.title: The Baker's Boy
chapters.summary: August's POV. Tomas, the baker's son who once swept the workshop, is arrested on information the ledger contains. August says nothing and hates themselves for it. Beat: the first true price of survival — complicity through silence.

chapters.title: Ink Under Orders
chapters.summary: August's POV. August begins producing the army's campaign maps by day, deliberately slow, while secretly planning how to alter the atlas. They test falsifying one plate and find Renn's clerk checks every line. Beat: trapped precision — the same skill that keeps them alive keeps them caged.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Reads Backwards
chapters.summary: Clerk Imre Voss's POV. Voss, a meticulous, lonely man, suspects the apprentice is hiding something and begins copying the ledger for himself. He is not cruel — only certain that accuracy is virtue. Beat: the banality of the collaborator's conscience.

chapters.title: Ice on the Pilings
chapters.summary: August's POV. The river ice thickens; the town's escape and supply route will close entirely, and the spring break will bring the army's barge reinforcements. August sets a private deadline: the atlas must be finished and the ledger gone before the ice breaks. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: What Odile Died For
chapters.summary: August's POV, with flashback. August remembers how Master Ferran was killed — not for treason but for refusing to hand over her field notes — and rereads her marginalia: the atlas was meant to be published, to make the province's hidden powers visible and accountable. Beat: grief converted to purpose.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Archive
chapters.summary: August and Voss's alternating POV. August offers Voss a deal: let one plate 'go missing' and August will correct an error that would disgrace Voss's own hometown section. Voss hesitates, tempted. Beat: two survivors circling each other, each measuring the other's price.

chapters.title: The General's Inspection
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. The General Staff arrives early; Renn, panicking, demands the atlas finished in days. August volunteers to 'finish it faster alone,' buying nights in the workshop. Beat: Renn's corruption deepens — he forges the General's preliminary approval to save himself.

chapters.title: Nights of the True Map
chapters.summary: August's POV. Working by shuttered lamplight, August completes the atlas as Odile intended — honest roads, honest names, honest debts — while the army's version grows flattering and false by day. Beat: identity crystallizing; August realizes they are no longer an apprentice but the map's author.

chapters.title: Voss Makes His Copy
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss finishes his private transcription of the ledger, telling himself it's for the record. Renn nearly catches him; Voss lies smoothly for the first time in his life and is shaken by how easy it was. Beat: corruption touches even the honest clerk.

chapters.title: Tomas Returns
chapters.summary: August's POV. Tomas escapes custody, half-frozen, and August hides him in the map chest room. Tomas knows the river ice's weak points from years of deliveries. Beat: debt repaid begins — August's survival now requires risking someone else's.

chapters.title: The Cracking Begins
chapters.summary: August's POV. The ice groans and shifts; the town whispers of the break. Renn orders the finished atlas sealed and loaded for the barge. August realizes the army's copy must be destroyed, not just evaded — a true copy in Renn's hands still dooms the names. Beat: escalation from evasion to sabotage.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss discovers Renn has falsified the General's approval and that the ledger will be used for reprisals, not record-keeping. He leaves his transcription where August will find it, with a single word: 'Burn.' Beat: the clerk's redemption through surrender of his own certainty.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: August's POV. August inks the final plate — the map of Vellamarch itself, every name restored — as soldiers hammer crates in the yard. Tomas marks the ice route; Voss falsifies the manifest to buy one night. Beat: the calm before the break, everything staked on a single night.

chapters.title: Night of the Break
chapters.summary: August and Renn's alternating POV. The ice splits with cannon-shot cracks; under its cover, August and Tomas sledge the true atlas and ledger to the far bank and the rival press at Osterlin. Renn discovers the theft mid-celebration. Beat: the climax begins — pursuit onto the breaking river.

chapters.title: White Water
chapters.summary: August's POV. The ice heaves; a floe separates August from the sledge. Tomas goes into the water saving the ledger; August hauls him out, losing the army's forged seal impression — their only leverage — to the river instead. Beat: sacrifice on the ice; what is saved and what is paid.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Workshop
chapters.summary: Renn's POV. Renn, unable to admit theft, declares the atlas destroyed by saboteurs and burns the workshop to hide his forged approval. Voss watches and says nothing, then quietly resigns his post. Beat: power devouring itself; the fire that erases August's old life.

chapters.title: The Press at Osterlin
chapters.summary: August's POV. At Osterlin, the rival cartographer prints the atlas as Odile intended — with August Whitlock's name on the title page, the first time August has signed anything. Copies spread before the army can react. Beat: triumph and exposure — visibility is the point, and the danger.

chapters.title: The Map Without a Master
chapters.summary: August's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, Vellamarch's names are public, reprisals stalled by scandal, Tomas baking again, Voss a schoolteacher in a far town. August, no longer hiding, begins a new map of the thawing river. Beat: resolution — identity chosen, price paid, the work outliving its makers.
